item.title: When will it stop raining in the UK? Met Office and BBC Weather reveals all
item.description: The UK has received plenty of rain during the early part of 2026, and the Met Office and BBC Weather have shared when it will stop

item.title: Gwynedd Council ‘extremely disappointed’ as second homes challenge fails
item.description: Gwynedd Council has failed in its appeal against a High Court decision to quash a ruling made on second/holiday homes in the county.

item.title: Anglesey father who died in A5025 crash 'would do anything for anybody'
item.description: The family of a man who died following a crash on Anglesey have paid tribute to him.

item.title: Anglesey: Company awarded Wylfa nuclear power plant contract worth £25million
item.description: A £25million contract has been awarded for a project which will deliver a new nuclear power plant on Anglesey.

item.title: Menai Suspension Bridge closes following crash as van appears to hit barrier
item.description: The Menai Suspension Bridge has closed to all vehicles following a crash.

item.title: 'I am heartbroken' - Family pay tribute to beloved man who died in crash
item.description: The family of a man who died following a crash on Anglesey have paid tribute to him.

item.title: North Wales women-led walking community set to climb Ben Nevis for charity
item.description: The founder of Wander Women is set to climb Ben Nevis with 15 other women this May to raise funds and awareness for the Domestic Abuse Safety Unit.

item.title: Reform UK threatens to defund Bangor University over student society Q&A refusal
item.description: "We are proud to be the first of the debating unions to take a stand against Reform UK. We strongly implore our fellow societies to join us."

item.title: Gwynedd moves closer to 2027 visitor charge in face of growing controversy
item.description: Gwynedd is preparing to take a major step toward introducing a new overnight visitor charge, with a 2027 launch on the table and millions in potential income at stake as councillors weigh up the next phase of the controversial plan.

item.title: Councillors give full support to plans for new duty free building at Holyhead Port
item.description: Councillors have unanimously approved plans for a new duty free building at Holyhead port, replacing ageing temporary cabins with a safer, better‑designed facility for ferry passengers.
